newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Group bids 720-730 ATS a share for CA - report.
newsitem.headline: Group bids 720-730 ATS a share for CA - report.

text.p: A consortium led by insurer EA-Generali has bid 720-730 schillings a share for two-thirds of the Austrian government's stake in Creditanstalt Bankverein, according to a magazine report.
No one from EA-Generali was immediately available for comment on the article from Thursday's edition of business weekly Wirtschaftswoche, obtained in advance by Reuters.
A finance ministry spokesman also declined to confirm the report, which named Citibank and BankAmerica Corp of the United States as additional suitors for Creditanstalt.
Creditanstalt ordinary shares were trading 0.9 schillings up at 730 on Wednesday.
The six-year privatisation of Austria's flagship bank entered a two to three week due diligence period on Monday. Afterwards potential investors must submit their final bids.
The finance ministry says it has received a host of indicative offers for its 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary voting shares but has refused to reveal details.

Wirtschaftswoche said the Austrian-Italian-German group, which includes savings bank Die Erste, Germany's Commerzbank and Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana, had put up 9.6 billion schillings for 13 million of the state's 19.9 million shares.
That would give the group around 45 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary voting shares. It would acquire a narrow majority by including EA-Generali's existing five percent stake, the magazine said.

Creditanstalt has topped the government's privatisation list since 1991. According to current market prices, the government's stake is worth some 14.5 billion schillings. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
